scope: Full QA failures and controlled old/current replays. Uniformly scaled monotonic-clock experiments simulate less compute within the same deadline; their reported virtual seconds are not measured CPU/browser latency. Crops and source-mask identities remain fixed. No success threshold is relaxed.

candle: test required the obsolete uncertain-candidate route

focusedFollowup.qualification: These do not replace the failed full suite. The candle now requires final geometry and paper validity, 1+1 cuts and the same independent image-error bound. Near-miss checks retain their original criteria and have clearer failure reports.

rootCause: The normal old/current replays pass all four photo targets. None runs the new clearance comparison.

At a 1.5x monotonic clock, both unchanged and current engines skip the feature initializer and reject all four. Initial three fine-grid counts, phases, 150-step errors and original mask hashes match the normal current run.
The feature initializer requires more than 3.5 seconds AFTER clearance/polishing reserves. In a ten-second request this effectively requires reaching that decision before about 2.7 seconds.
After skipping the useful start, the solver instead spends roughly five virtual seconds on unsuccessful MILP recovery. Returning to ordinary grids cannot recover the missing source region.
A separate local-shape issue remains: whole-image acceptance can pass while the sun-window test fails. It is retained in prototype scoring.
